selected.he_nikud: נב) קֹדֶם שֶׁאָמַר רַבֵּנוּ זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה הַתּוֹרָה הַנִּדְפֶּסֶת בְּלִקּוּטֵי תִּנְיָנָא בְּסִימָן ל"ב הַמַּתְחֶלֶת יֵשׁ צַדִּיקִים גְּנוּזִים, וְנֶאֶמְרָה בְּשַׁבָּת פָּרָשַׁת יִתְרוֹ תקס"ט לפ"ק [לִפְרָט קָטָן]. וְסִפֵּר מַעֲשֶׂה מִקֹּדֶם שֶׁהַבַּעַל־שֵׁם־טוֹב זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה הָיָה בִּקְהִלַּת־קֹדֶשׁ בְּרָאד וְנִתְאַכְסֵן אֵצֶל גְּבִיר אֶחָד וְהָיוּ מְסֻבִּין שָׁם עַל הַשֻּׁלְחָן אֲנָשִׁים רַבִּים מְכֻבָּדִים לִכְבוֹדוֹ כַּנָּהוּג, וְהָיָה יוֹשֵׁב שָׁם לְמַטָּה אֵצֶל הַשֻּׁלְחָן בַּעַל דַּרְשֶׁיר אֶחָד הַיְנוּ דַּרְשָׁן. וְהָיָה אוֹכֵל הַרְבֵּה, וְהִסְתַּכְּלוּ עָלָיו שֶׁאוֹכֵל הַרְבֵּה מְאֹד, וְהִתְחִילוּ לִתֵּן לוֹ וּלְהוֹשִׁיט לוֹ אֲכִילָה הַרְבֵּה בִּשְׁבִיל לֵיצָנוּת. וְהַדַּרְשָׁן עָשָׂה אֶת שֶׁלּוֹ, וְאָכַל הַרְבֵּה כָּל מַה שֶּׁהוֹשִׁיטוּ לוֹ כְּגוֹן דָּגִים שֶׁהָיוּ אוֹכְלִים שְׁנֵי אֲנָשִׁים חֲתִיכָה אַחַת וְהַדַּרְשָׁן אָכַל בְּעַצְמוֹ שְׁתֵּי חֲתִיכוֹת דָּגִים, וְכֵן רֹטֶב שֶׁהָיָה אוֹכֵל בְּעַצְמוֹ קְעָרָה מְלֵאָה וְכֵן בִּשְׁאָר הַמַּאֲכָלִים וְהֵם הוֹשִׁיטוּ לוֹ בְּכָל פַּעַם בִּשְׁבִיל לֵיצָנוּת מֵחֲמַת שֶׁרָאוּ שֶׁאוֹכֵל הַרְבֵּה.
selected.en: (52.) Before Rabbainu, of blessed memory, said the Torah printed in Likutay Tinyana, section 32, which begins "There are hidden tzaddikim," and was said on the Sabbath of the Torah portion Yisro, 5569, le-frat katan [minor era]—he related a story from earlier times: the Baal Shem Tov, of blessed memory, was in the holy community of Brod and lodged with a certain wealthy man, and many distinguished people were reclining there at the table in his honor, as is customary. And sitting there lower down at the table was a certain baal darshir, that is, a preacher. And he was eating much, and they watched him eating very much, and began to give him and to hand him much food for mockery. And the preacher went on with what he was doing and ate much, everything that they handed him—such as fish: two people would eat one piece, while the preacher ate two pieces of fish by himself; and likewise broth, of which he would eat a full bowl by himself, and likewise with the other foods. And they handed him [food] each time for mockery, because they saw that he ate much.

selected.translationSourceEnglish: (52.) Before Rabbainu o.b.m. said the Torah printed in Likutay Moharan, vol. 2, Torah 32 — which begins "There are hidden tzaddikim," and was said on the Sabbath of the Torah portion Yisro, 5569 [1809] in the minor era — he told the following story: The Baal Shem Tov o.b.m. was once in the holy community of Brod, and was lodging by a certain wealthy man, and many distinguished people were reclining there at the table in his honor as is customary. And sitting there at the bottom of the table was a certain preacher [darshan]. And he was eating a great deal, and they looked at him and saw that he was eating very much, and began to give him and extend to him food amply, as a joke. And the preacher did what he did, and ate a great deal of everything that was extended to him — such as fish, where two people would eat one portion, the preacher ate two portions himself; and similarly soup — he himself ate a full bowl; and so too with the other foods. And they extended to him each time as a joke, because they saw that he ate a great deal.

retained_baseline.en: And immediately he began to cry out "Woe and alas" over the great pain of all his limbs, and cried out bitterly, detailed account by account, over the pain of each and every limb — for the bones of each and every limb began to break, which they call brekhin in Yiddish — and cried out in this manner from within his illness for some time until he died, as the Baal Shem Tov o.b.m. had said. And one who peruses the discourse "Anochi" mentioned above will well understand the matter of this story. (59.) The chronological order of the recitation of the discourses known to us: The discourse "Akruktah" (Likutay Moharan, Torah 3) — I heard that it was said on the first Sabbath that Rabbainu o.b.m. entered Breslov, at the end of the year 5562 [1801/2]. The discourse "Anochi" (Torah 4) — was said in Zlatipoleye on Shavuos. The discourse "With Trumpets" (Torah 5) — was said on Rosh Hashana 5563 [1802]. The discourse "Call Joshua" (Torah 6) — was said on Shabbos Teshuva that followed. The discourse "Mishpatim" (Torah 7) — was said in the winter of 5563. The discourse "I saw a golden menorah" (Torah 8) — was said on the Sabbath of Chanuka 5563. The discourse "The depths will cover them" (Torah 9) — was said on Shabbat Shira 5563. The discourse "Mishpatim" (Torah 10) — was also said in that same winter, in Tiraovitze, before Purim.

selected.en: Afterwards they began to urge him to say Torah before them. And their intention was also mockery: that he should say Torah at the table where the Baal Shem Tov, of blessed memory, was reclining at the head. And he conducted himself in his simplicity and began to say Torah before them, and they began to laugh at him into the palms of their hands, and he was in their eyes an object of laughter and mockery [laughter and mockery]. And the preacher understood that they were mocking him because he was eating much; the preacher answered and said: "And if one cannot say Torah, is it forbidden to eat a piece of fish?" Afterwards the Baal Shem Tov looked and saw the whole matter and took exception and became angry with them, and heard the preacher’s Torah, and it was very good in his eyes. And the Baal Shem Tov said that this preacher says Torah from the mouth of Elijah, of blessed memory. All this Rabbainu, of blessed memory, related.

The discourse "Seal within seal" (Torah 22) — was said in the week after Rosh Hashana 5565.

selected.en: (53.) In 5568, close to Rosh Hashana, we traveled with him outside the city, I and my companion Rabbi Naftoli. And he related that he had dreamed that they were conversing that healing is from Hashem, blessed be He, alone, for "I am Hashem your healer." And only Hashem, blessed be He, can heal. And they said: "Who knows that Hashem, blessed be He, wishes [to heal]?" And one of us two answered—and he [Rabbainu] did not wish to say who the one was—"Ki ani Hashem rofecha" ("For I am Hashem your healer") indicates this, for it forms the initial letters of "Amen ken yehi ratzon" ("Amen, so may it be [His] will"), as printed in Likutay Tinyana, section 42.

selected.en: (54) He spoke with us concerning the Torah printed in Likutey Tinyana, section 40, which begins: One who knows of the Land of Israel, who has truly tasted the taste of the Land of Israel, and said that he had known this long before, for, after all, I traveled to the Land of Israel, and presumably I had previously had a desire and yearning to travel to the Land of Israel, and I also dreamed of the Land of Israel. And once a certain man was with me, and I spoke with him, and a great yearning and desire for the Land of Israel began to awaken within me. And afterward I asked him whether he had been with tzaddikim on Rosh Hashana, and he told me that he had been with several great, true tzaddikim on Rosh Hashana, and because of this I had great yearning when I spoke with him, as explained in the aforementioned Torah.

selected.translationSourceEnglish: (54.) He spoke with us about the matter of the Torah printed in Likutay Moharan, vol. 2, Torah 40 — which begins: "One who knows about the Land of Israel, who has truly tasted the taste of the Land of Israel" — and he said that he had known this from before, for had he not traveled to the Land of Israel? And presumably he had had longing and yearning before that to travel to the Land of Israel, and he had also dreamed of the Land of Israel. And one time there was a certain man with him, and he spoke with him, and there arose in him a great longing and desire for the Land of Israel. And afterwards he asked him if he had been by tzaddikim for Rosh Hashana, and he told him that he had been by several great true tzaddikim for Rosh Hashana — and on account of this he had great yearning when he spoke with him, as is explained in the aforementioned Torah.

retained_baseline.en: The discourses "Three depart" and "The Holy Sanctuary" (Torahs 58 and 59) — were said on Rosh Hashana 5566 [1805]. The discourse "Rabbi Shimon opened" (Torah 60) — was said on Rosh Hashana 5567 [1806]. The discourse "Rabbi Shimon rejoiced" (Torah 61) — was said on Rosh Hashana 5568 [1807]. The discourse "And G‑d led" (Torah 62) — was said on Shabbat Shira 5565. The discourse "The secret of the intention of the milah" (Torah 63) — was said on the Sabbath before the bris milah of his holy son Shlomo Ephraim of blessed memory, who was born close to Rosh Chodesh Nisan 5565. The discourse "And Boaz said to Ruth" (Torah 65) — was said in the summer of 5566, close after the passing of his holy son Shlomo Ephraim mentioned above, which was in the month of Sivan 5566 — and then the aforementioned discourse was said on a Friday, the eve of the holy Sabbath. And before it he said the discourse "Know that there is an Orech Anpin" etc. (Torah 242), and on the Thursday before that he wept before us.

selected.translationSourceEnglish: And he said to me: even though he knew this matter before, he did not know it at all as he knows it now. For then he knew only this alone — that because one speaks with a person who was by a true tzaddik for Rosh Hashana, one who longs for the Land of Israel should feel [the taste of] the Land of Israel. But the inner matter of the thing — from where this derives — he did not know at all as he now knows it. For now he merited that it was revealed to him in its completeness. And he said to me: Even though he had known this matter before, he did not know it at all in comparison to what he knows now — for now he knows the matter completely in its revelation. And in all this matter writing instruments are insufficient to explain the matter well, and the discerning ones will understand a little of themselves.

retained_baseline.en: And on the Sabbath that followed he said the discourse "And my drink I have mingled with weeping" (Torah 262). The discourse "And let there be two" (Torah 66) — was said after Chanuka 5567. And on the Sabbath it was said [the portion] regarding the breaking of impediments explained there. selected.en: (55) And likewise, the matter of the twenty-four kinds of pidyonos (redemptions) needed to sweeten the twenty-four courts of judgment, printed in Likutey I, section 215—he already knew of this before he was in the Land of Israel. As I heard from our fellowship, and particularly from one distinguished man of our fellowship, who related that once his wife became ill and was literally close to death; her soul had almost departed. And he came to him, of blessed memory, and [the latter] said to him: Run quickly and bring twenty-four pidyonos before the verdict is decreed and sealed. And he ran and brought him a sack full of money. And afterward a miracle occurred and she returned to her health, and afterward our Rabbi, of blessed memory, commanded that all the money be returned to him, only to accept twenty-four gedolim [a type of coin] and distribute them to the poor.

retained_baseline.en: The discourse "And He built the rib" (Torah 67) — was said in Zaslav on Shavuos 5567. The discourse "To strengthen oneself each time against the evil inclination" (Torah 72) — was said at the time that his holy son Shlomo Ephraim mentioned above was born. The discourse "And He will give might to His king" (Torah 78) — was said in Zlatipoleye on Rosh Hashana 5561 [1800]. The discourse "A wicked person plots against the tzaddik" (Torah 96) — was said a long time before his journey to the Land of Israel. The discourse "A light — make for the ark" (Torah 112) — was said at the beginning of the winter of 5563. The discourses "A spring that issues from one place" and "And the path of the righteous" (Torahs 132 and 133) — were said after Pesach 5563, upon his return from the journey to the wedding of his daughter Sara of blessed memory. The discourse "In Your Name they will rejoice" etc. (Torah 175) — was said on the night after Shabbos Teshuva [the Sabbath of Repentance] 5565. Note on Article 59

selected.en: And then he also spoke of how it is impossible to perform a pidyon except when one knows all twenty-four kinds of pidyonos, to sweeten all twenty-four courts of judgment. And he gave a parable: as when a claim is brought against someone in the guberniye [government] of Kiev, and he appoints an advocate, called a filiptent, in Kaminitz. Thus, how is it possible to perform a pidyon if one does not know in which courts of judgment they are judging him?

selected.he: ואמר אז גם כן שיש פדיון גבוה כל כך שיכול להמתיק כל העשרים וארבעה בתי דינין, ועוד יש בזה כמה שיחות מכבר, אבל לא ידע אז כל הענין בשלמות כאשר ידע אחר כך, כאשר גלה קצת מזה לנו שלפעמים גם בזה הפדיון שכולל כל העשרים וארבעה בתי דינין, אף על פי כן אינו מועיל כי נעשה מזה ענין אחר הינו גרים, וזה בחינת משה שעומד בין שמד לרצון כל זה לא ידע אז, רק אחר כך על ידי עבודתו שיגע ועבד בכל עת עד שהגיע בכל פעם למדרגות גבוהות עליונות יותר, ואז השיג והבין בהתגלות נפלא מה שידע מתחלה בסתם, בבחינת העלם רק ברמז.
selected.he_nikud: וְאָמַר אָז גַּם־כֵּן שֶׁיֵּשׁ פִּדְיוֹן גָּבוֹהַּ כָּל כָּךְ שֶׁיָּכוֹל לְהַמְתִּיק כָּל הָעֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה בָּתֵּי דִינִין, וְעוֹד יֵשׁ בָּזֶה כַּמָּה שִׂיחוֹת מִכְּבָר, אֲבָל לֹא יָדַע אָז כָּל הָעִנְיָן בִּשְׁלֵמוּת כַּאֲשֶׁר יָדַע אַחַר־כָּךְ, כַּאֲשֶׁר גִּלָּה קְצָת מִזֶּה לָנוּ שֶׁלִּפְעָמִים גַּם בְּזֶה הַפִּדְיוֹן שֶׁכּוֹלֵל כָּל הָעֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה בָּתֵּי דִינִין, אַף־עַל־פִּי־כֵן אֵינוֹ מוֹעִיל כִּי נַעֲשֶׂה מִזֶּה עִנְיָן אַחֵר הַיְנוּ גֵּרִים, וְזֶה בְּחִינַת מֹשֶׁה שֶׁעוֹמֵד בֵּין שְׁמָד לְרָצוֹן כָּל זֶה לֹא יָדַע אָז, רַק אַחַר־כָּךְ עַל־יְדֵי עֲבוֹדָתוֹ שֶׁיָּגַע וְעָבַד בְּכָל עֵת עַד שֶׁהִגִּיעַ בְּכָל פַּעַם לְמַדְרֵגוֹת גְּבוֹהוֹת עֶלְיוֹנוֹת יוֹתֵר, וְאָז הִשִּׂיג וְהֵבִין בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת נִפְלָא מַה שֶּׁיָּדַע מִתְּחִלָּה בִּסְתָם, בִּבְחִינַת הֶעְלֵם רַק בְּרֶמֶז.
selected.en: And he also said then that there is a pidyon so exalted that it can sweeten all twenty-four courts of judgment, and there are several further conversations about this from earlier, but he did not then know the entire matter in its completeness as he knew it afterward, as he revealed a little of this to us: that sometimes, even with this pidyon which encompasses all twenty-four courts of judgment, it nevertheless does not avail, because a different matter comes about from this, namely converts, and this is the aspect of Moses, who stands between shmad (apostasy) and ratzon (favor). All this he did not know then, but only afterward, through his service, in which he toiled and labored at all times until each time he reached higher, more exalted levels; and then he attained and understood, in wondrous revelation, what he had known at first in an unspecified way, in an aspect of concealment, only by allusion.

selected.translationSourceEnglish: And he also said then that there is a pidyon so elevated that it can sweeten all twenty-four courts of law. And there are in this matter many additional conversations from before — but he did not then know the entire matter in its completeness as he knew it afterwards. For then he knew only this: that sometimes even this pidyon that encompasses all twenty-four courts of law is nevertheless insufficient, because through it a different matter arises — namely, converts — and this is the aspect of Moses who stands between apostasy and [Divine] favor. All this he did not know then — only afterwards, through his service [of G‑d] in which he toiled and labored at all times, until he arrived each time at ever higher and more exalted levels — he then attained and understood in a wondrous revelation what he had previously known vaguely, in a hidden way, only by allusion.

retained_baseline.he: ואמר אז גם כן שיש פדיון גבוה כל כך שיכול להמתיק כל העשרים וארבעה בתי דינין, ועוד יש בזה כמה שיחות מכבר, אבל לא ידע אז כל הענין בשלמות כאשר ידע אחר כך, כאשר גלה קצת מזה לנו שלפעמים גם בזה הפדיון שכולל כל העשרים וארבעה בתי דינין, אף על פי כן אינו מועיל כי נעשה מזה ענין אחר הינו גרים, וזה בחינת משה שעומד בין שמד לרצון כל זה לא ידע אז, רק אחר כך על ידי עבודתו שיגע ועבד בכל עת עד שהגיע בכל פעם למדרגות גבוהות עליונות יותר, ואז השיג והבין בהתגלות נפלא מה שידע מתחלה בסתם, בבחינת העלם רק ברמז.
retained_baseline.en: The passage about hisbodidus — "Give your hearts to me and I will lead you on a new path" — cited in numerous Breslov sources under article 59 is drawn from a separate section of this book and is presented here as a cross-reference. It is found in its proper place within the Hisbodidus section of Sichos HaRan and is referenced throughout the book. The Tikun Klali (General Rectification — the ten Psalms: 16, 32, 41, 42, 59, 77, 90, 105, 137, 150) is documented in Likutay Moharan vol. 1, §205; vol. 2, §92; Sefer Hamidos, Nocturnal Emission 5; Sichos HaRan 141; and this book at articles 59, 162, 184, and 225. General article count: 60 onward  |  Section count: 1 onward The discourse "To strengthen oneself each time against the evil inclination" (Torah 72) — was said at the time that his holy son Shlomo Ephraim mentioned above was born. General article count: 60 onward  |  Section count: 1 onward [Continued in the next section — Articles beginning with #60] Sections II, III & IV — Conversations Pertaining to the Legendary Tales · the Book of Attributes · New Stories Conversations Pertaining to the Legendary Tales
retained_baseline.he_nikud: וְאָמַר אָז גַּם־כֵּן שֶׁיֵּשׁ פִּדְיוֹן גָּבוֹהַּ כָּל כָּךְ שֶׁיָּכוֹל לְהַמְתִּיק כָּל הָעֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה בָּתֵּי דִינִין, וְעוֹד יֵשׁ בָּזֶה כַּמָּה שִׂיחוֹת מִכְּבָר, אֲבָל לֹא יָדַע אָז כָּל הָעִנְיָן בִּשְׁלֵמוּת כַּאֲשֶׁר יָדַע אַחַר־כָּךְ, כַּאֲשֶׁר גִּלָּה קְצָת מִזֶּה לָנוּ שֶׁלִּפְעָמִים גַּם בְּזֶה הַפִּדְיוֹן שֶׁכּוֹלֵל כָּל הָעֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה בָּתֵּי דִינִין, אַף־עַל־פִּי־כֵן אֵינוֹ מוֹעִיל כִּי נַעֲשֶׂה מִזֶּה עִנְיָן אַחֵר הַיְנוּ גֵּרִים, וְזֶה בְּחִינַת מֹשֶׁה שֶׁעוֹמֵד בֵּין שְׁמָד לְרָצוֹן כָּל זֶה לֹא יָדַע אָז, רַק אַחַר־כָּךְ עַל־יְדֵי עֲבוֹדָתוֹ שֶׁיָּגַע וְעָבַד בְּכָל עֵת עַד שֶׁהִגִּיעַ בְּכָל פַּעַם לְמַדְרֵגוֹת גְּבוֹהוֹת עֶלְיוֹנוֹת יוֹתֵר, וְאָז הִשִּׂיג וְהֵבִין בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת נִפְלָא מַה שֶּׁיָּדַע מִתְּחִלָּה בִּסְתָם, בִּבְחִינַת הֶעְלֵם רַק בְּרֶמֶז.

selected.he: ומזה תוכל להבין מעט מקצת גדלתו כי גם מקדם היה חדוש נפלא חד בדרא, כי אמר שמאלו העשרים וארבעה פדיונות אינו יודע כי אם חד בדרא. וכל זה היה קדם ארץ ישראל ואחר כך כשבא מארץ ישראל אמר שהוא מתביש בכל התורות וההשגות שהשיג קדם שהיה בארץ ישראל ולא היו נחשבים בעיניו לכלום. ראה והבן עד היכן עלה אחר כך, ויש בענין זה לדבר הרבה איך גם קדם ארץ ישראל היה חדוש נפלא כשידע מהעשרים וארבעה מיני פדיונות, או מענין ארץ ישראל הנ"ל כמו שהיה יודע אז, אך אף על פי כן נגד הידיעה שידע אחר כך ענינים אלו בעצמם כמו שידעם אחר כך אין הידיעה הראשונה נחשבת לכלום, כפי אשר הבנתי מדעתו הקדושה אך בכל ענין זה אין כלי הכתיבה מספיקים להסביר הענין היטב, והמשכילים יבינו מעט מאליהם:
selected.he_nikud: וּמִזֶּה תּוּכַל לְהָבִין מְעַט מִקְצָת גְּדֻלָּתוֹ כִּי גַּם מִקֹּדֶם הָיָה חִדּוּשׁ נִפְלָא חָד בְּדָרָא, כִּי אָמַר שֶׁמֵּאֵלּוּ הָעֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה פִּדְיוֹנוֹת אֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ כִּי־אִם חָד בְּדָרָא. וְכָל זֶה הָיָה קֹדֶם אֶרֶץ־יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאַחַר־כָּךְ כְּשֶׁבָּא מֵאֶרֶץ־יִשְׂרָאֵל אָמַר שֶׁהוּא מִתְבַּיֵּשׁ בְּכָל הַתּוֹרוֹת וְהַהַשָּׂגוֹת שֶׁהִשִּׂיג קֹדֶם שֶׁהָיָה בְּאֶרֶץ־יִשְׂרָאֵל וְלֹא הָיוּ נֶחְשָׁבִים בְּעֵינָיו לִכְלוּם. רְאֵה וְהָבֵן עַד הֵיכָן עָלָה אַחַר־כָּךְ, וְיֵשׁ בְּעִנְיָן זֶה לְדַבֵּר הַרְבֵּה אֵיךְ גַּם קֹדֶם אֶרֶץ־יִשְׂרָאֵל הָיָה חִדּוּשׁ נִפְלָא כְּשֶׁיָּדַע מֵהָעֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה מִינֵי פִּדְיוֹנוֹת, אוֹ מֵעִנְיַן אֶרֶץ־יִשְׂרָאֵל הַנַּ"ל כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה יוֹדֵעַ אָז, אַךְ אַף־עַל־פִּי־כֵן נֶגֶד הַיְדִיעָה שֶׁיָּדַע אַחַר־כָּךְ עִנְיָנִים אֵלּוּ בְּעַצְמָם כְּמוֹ שֶׁיְּדָעָם אַחַר־כָּךְ אֵין הַיְדִיעָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה נֶחְשֶׁבֶת לִכְלוּם, כְּפִי אֲשֶׁר הֵבַנְתִּי מִדַּעְתּוֹ הַקְּדוֹשָׁה אַךְ בְּכָל עִנְיָן זֶה אֵין כְּלֵי הַכְּתִיבָה מַסְפִּיקִים לְהַסְבִּיר הָעִנְיָן הֵיטֵב, וְהַמַּשְׂכִּילִים יָבִינוּ מְעַט מֵאֲלֵיהֶם:
selected.en: And from this you can understand a little of a fraction of his greatness, for even earlier he was a wondrous novelty, chad bedara (one in a generation), for he said that only one in a generation knows of these twenty-four pidyonos. And all this was before the Land of Israel, and afterward, when he came from the Land of Israel, he said that he was ashamed of all the Torah teachings and attainments that he had attained before he was in the Land of Israel, and they counted for nothing in his eyes. See and understand how far he ascended afterward, and there is much to say about this matter: how even before the Land of Israel he was a wondrous novelty when he knew of the twenty-four kinds of pidyonos, or of the aforementioned matter of the Land of Israel as he knew it then; but nevertheless, compared with the knowledge by which he afterward knew these very matters, as he knew them afterward, the earlier knowledge counts for nothing, according to what I understood from his holy mind. But in this entire matter the instruments of writing are insufficient to explain the matter well, and the discerning will understand a little on their own:

selected.translationSourceEnglish: And from this you can understand a little of a fraction of his greatness. For even before [his journey to the Land of Israel] he was already an unprecedented wondrous novelty — for he said that of these twenty-four types of pidyonos, he knew only that which is known once in a generation (chad b'dara). And all this was before the Land of Israel. And afterwards when he returned from the Land of Israel, he said that he was ashamed of all the Torahs and attainments he had attained before being in the Land of Israel, and they were as nothing in his eyes. See and understand how high he rose afterwards — and there is much to say about this matter: how even before the Land of Israel he was an unprecedented wondrous novelty when he knew the twenty-four types of pidyonos, or the matter of the Land of Israel as he knew it then. Yet even still, against the knowledge with which he afterwards knew those very same matters — as he knew them afterwards — the earlier knowledge was as nothing, as I have understood from his holy mind. But in all this matter, writing instruments are insufficient to explain the matter well, and the discerning ones will understand a little of themselves.

retained_baseline.he: ומזה תוכל להבין מעט מקצת גדלתו כי גם מקדם היה חדוש נפלא חד בדרא, כי אמר שמאלו העשרים וארבעה פדיונות אינו יודע כי אם חד בדרא. וכל זה היה קדם ארץ ישראל ואחר כך כשבא מארץ ישראל אמר שהוא מתביש בכל התורות וההשגות שהשיג קדם שהיה בארץ ישראל ולא היו נחשבים בעיניו לכלום. ראה והבן עד היכן עלה אחר כך, ויש בענין זה לדבר הרבה איך גם קדם ארץ ישראל היה חדוש נפלא כשידע מהעשרים וארבעה מיני פדיונות, או מענין ארץ ישראל הנ"ל כמו שהיה יודע אז, אך אף על פי כן נגד הידיעה שידע אחר כך ענינים אלו בעצמם כמו שידעם אחר כך אין הידיעה הראשונה נחשבת לכלום, כפי אשר הבנתי מדעתו הקדושה אך בכל ענין זה אין כלי הכתיבה מספיקים להסביר הענין היטב, והמשכילים יבינו מעט מאליהם:

selected.he: (נו) ראה זה מצאתי מכתב יד רבנו זכרונו לברכה בעצמו מענין התורה ויבן לו בית בסימן רס"ו דע כשהעולם פוגמין במצות סכה כשאין מקימין אותה כראוי גורמין מיתה או חולאת לבהמות ולשאר בעלי חיים הכל לפי הפגם. כי זה ההפרש שבין בני האדם ובין בעלי חיים כי שפעם של בני אדם יונקים ממקום בינה, כמאמר חכמינו זכרונם לברכה (ברכות י): שעשה לה דדים במקום בינה, מה שאין כן בעלי חיים, ששפעם יונקים ממקום הערוה. ובחינת סכה היא בחינת אמא בינה דמסככא על בנהא ואנו יונקים ממנה, ובזאת המצוה אנו מבדלים משפע של בעלי חיים. וכשפוגמין במצות סכה אזי יורדין על ידי זה ממדרגת בני אדם, ואין להם שפע ממקום בינה, ויורדין למדרגות שאר בעלי חיים. ונדחין שאר בעלי חיים מהשפע שלהם, כיון שבני אדם לוקחין השפע שלהם, ואזי הבעלי החיים מתים או נופלים בחלאים הכל לפי לקיחת השפע שלהם אם רב אם מעט, וזהו (בראשית ל"ג) ולמקנהו עשה סכת. הינו כי סכות הוא חיים וקיום לבעלי חיים שישארו על מדרגתם כנ"ל. וכשבני אדם יושבים בסכות כראוי, על ידי זה הם במדרגתן, ובבחינת תורה. כי התורה היא בחינת (משלי א): "אל תטש תורת אמך", "אם לבינה תקרא". (שם ב) בשביל זה סמוך לסכות אנו עושים שמחת תורה. וזה סוון ראשי תבות ו'יעקב נ'סע ס'כותה ו'יבן כי בסיון נתנה תורה ואנו במדרגת התורה על ידי מצות סכה כנזכר לעיל:
selected.he_nikud: נו) רְאֵה זֶה מָצָאתִי מִכְּתַב יַד רַבֵּנוּ זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה בְּעַצְמוֹ מֵעִנְיַן הַתּוֹרָה וַיִּבֶן לוֹ בָּיִת בְּסִימָן רס"ו דַּע כְּשֶׁהָעוֹלָם פּוֹגְמִין בְּמִצְוַת סֻכָּה כְּשֶׁאֵין מְקַיְּמִין אוֹתָהּ כָּרָאוּי גּוֹרְמִין מִיתָה אוֹ חוֹלַאֲת לַבְּהֵמוֹת וְלִשְׁאָר בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים הַכֹּל לְפִי הַפְּגָם. כִּי זֶה הַהֶפְרֵשׁ שֶׁבֵּין בְּנֵי הָאָדָם וּבֵין בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים כִּי שִׁפְעָם שֶׁל בְּנֵי אָדָם יוֹנְקִים מִמְּקוֹם בִּינָה, כְּמַאֲמַר חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת י): שֶׁעָשָׂה לָהּ דַּדִּים בִּמְקוֹם בִּינָה, מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בַּעֲלֵי־חַיִּים, שֶׁשִּׁפְעָם יוֹנְקִים מִמְּקוֹם הָעֶרְוָה. וּבְחִינַת סֻכָּה הִיא בְּחִינַת אִמָּא בִּינָה דִּמְסָכְכָא עַל בְּנָהָא וְאָנוּ יוֹנְקִים מִמֶּנָּה, וּבְזֹאת הַמִּצְוָה אָנוּ מֻבְדָּלִים מִשֶּׁפַע שֶׁל בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים. וּכְשֶׁפּוֹגְמִין בְּמִצְוַת סֻכָּה אֲזַי יוֹרְדִין עַל־יְדֵי־זֶה מִמַּדְרֵגַת בְּנֵי אָדָם, וְאֵין לָהֶם שֶׁפַע מִמְּקוֹם בִּינָה, וְיוֹרְדִין לְמַדְרֵגוֹת שְׁאָר בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים. וְנִדָּחִין שְׁאָר בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים מֵהַשֶּׁפַע שֶׁלָּהֶם, כֵּיוָן שֶׁבְּנֵי אָדָם לוֹקְחִין הַשֶּׁפַע שֶׁלָּהֶם, וַאֲזַי הַבַּעֲלֵי הַחַיִּים מֵתִים אוֹ נוֹפְלִים בָּחֳלָאִים הַכֹּל לְפִי לְקִיחַת הַשֶּׁפַע שֶׁלָּהֶם אִם רַב אִם מְעָט, וְזֶהוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית ל"ג) וּלְמִקְנֵהוּ עָשָׂה סֻכֹּת. הַיְנוּ כִּי סֻכּוֹת הוּא חַיִּים וְקִיּוּם לְבַעֲלֵי חַיִּים שֶׁיִּשָּׁאֲרוּ עַל מַדְרֵגָתָם כַּנַּ"ל. וּכְשֶׁבְּנֵי אָדָם יוֹשְׁבִים בַּסֻּכּוֹת כָּרָאוּי, עַל־יְדֵי־זֶה הֵם בְּמַדְרֵגָתָן, וּבִבְחִינַת תּוֹרָה. כִּי הַתּוֹרָה הִיא בְּחִינַת (מִשְׁלֵי א): "אַל תִּטֹּשׁ תּוֹרַת אִמֶּךָ", "אִם לַבִּינָה תִּקְרָא". (שָׁם ב) בִּשְׁבִיל זֶה סָמוּךְ לְסֻכּוֹת אָנוּ עוֹשִׂים שִׂמְחַת תּוֹרָה. וְזֶה סִוָון רָאשֵׁי־תֵבוֹת וְ'יַעֲקֹב נָ'סַע סֻ'כּוֹתָה וַ'יִּבֶן כִּי בְּסִיוָן נִתְּנָה תּוֹרָה וְאָנוּ בְּמַדְרֵגַת הַתּוֹרָה עַל־יְדֵי מִצְוַת סֻכָּה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל:
selected.en: (56) See, this I found in the handwriting of our Rabbi, of blessed memory, himself, concerning the Torah ‘And he built himself a house,’ in section 266: Know: when the world blemishes the commandment of sukkah, when they do not fulfill it properly, they cause death or illness to the beasts and to the other living creatures, all according to the blemish. For this is the difference between human beings and living creatures, because human beings draw their bounty by nursing from the place of Binah (understanding), as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Berakhot 10): that He made breasts for her in the place of Binah; not so living creatures, who draw their bounty by nursing from the place of the private parts. And the aspect of sukkah is the aspect of Imma-Binah (Mother-Binah), who shelters over her children, and we nurse from her; and through this commandment we are distinguished from the bounty of living creatures. And when they blemish the commandment of sukkah, then through this they descend from the level of human beings, and they have no bounty from the place of Binah, and they descend to the levels of the other living creatures. And the other living creatures are thrust away from their bounty, since human beings take their bounty; and then the living creatures die or fall into illnesses, all according to the taking of their bounty, whether much or little. And this is (Genesis 33): ‘And for his livestock he made sukkos (booths).’ That is, sukkos is life and continued existence for living creatures, so that they remain at their level, as mentioned above. And when human beings sit in sukkos properly, through this they are at their level and in the aspect of Torah. For the Torah is the aspect of (Proverbs 1): ‘Do not forsake the Torah of your mother’; ‘If you call to Binah’ (ibid. 2). For this reason, close to Sukkos we celebrate Simchas Torah. And this is ‘סוון’ (Sivan), the initial letters of ו'יעקב נ'סע ס'כותה ו'יבן (‘And Jacob journeyed to Sukkos and built’), for in Sivan the Torah was given, and we are at the level of the Torah through the commandment of sukkah, as mentioned above:

editorial_apparatus.text: 56.189.1: AI editorial supplement, not authenticated original English. The narrator says I found and attributes the manuscript to the Rabbi himself; this is not modern authentication. Both witnesses give רס"ו (266) and do not print the work-name Likutay Moharan here. לו is rendered reflexively himself in the title. The differing marker parentheses remain unchanged. Independent review: The narrator, not the present editor, asserts discovery and handwriting attribution. Both witness markers stay exact.

56.189.2: Both witnesses retain world, repeated when, do not, death OR illness, beasts AND other living creatures, and all according to the blemish. This is the source’s theological causal assertion, not independently asserted biological fact; it is not softened or presented as medical guidance. Independent review: The causal link between ritual observance and animal illness is the source’s theological assertion, not an empirical endorsement or medical guidance.

56.189.3: Both Hebrew fields retain repeated bounty/nursing, human-versus-animal contrast, breasts, her, and private parts. Binah is the technical term with an understanding gloss, not silently replaced by intellect; secondary [the Sefirah of] is editorial expansion. The citation is exactly tractate and numeral10, with no folio side supplied. The capitalized He reflects the contextual divine maker, not an explicit Hebrew subject-name. Independent review: Because restores כי without changing agency. He refers contextually to the divine maker; that identification is not established by pointing alone. The source prints Berakhot10 without a folio side.

56.189.4: Both witnesses retain aspect twice, maternal Imma-Binah and Aramaic דמסככא על בנהא / דִּמְסָכְכָא עַל בְּנָהָא (shelters over her children), and we nurse from her. Pointed מֻבְדָּלִים supports are distinguished; unpointed מבדלים is preserved without normalization. Maternal/sukkah covering wordplay remains visible through shelters and the retained technical term. Independent review: The pointed witness supports passive are distinguished; the unpointed consonants remain exact. Shelters over makes the covering relation explicit without inventing an actor.

56.189.5: Both fields repeat descend, distinguish singular human level from plural animal levels, and explicitly negate access to bounty from Binah. Preserve plural agents rather than the secondary’s switch to singular one, and preserve then and through this. Independent review: No suppression of the negative or second descent; they remains plural and is not replaced with an invented named group.

56.189.6: Human taking causes animals’ loss in both witnesses; agency is not reversed. Repeated their bounty, all, whether much or little, and death/illness alternatives remain. Source citation is Genesis33 only, not secondary33:17. עשה / עָשָׂה means made here, not the secondary’s built; quote translated from supplied witnesses, not silently normalized. Independent review: Pronouns their refer contextually to creatures’ bounty; quotation and chapter-only citation are translated from these witnesses rather than normalized to an external edition.

56.189.7: Both witnesses retain life AND continued existence, creatures’ remaining at their own level, and כנ"ל / כַּנַּ"ל as mentioned above. No independent causal endorsement is implied. Independent review: The asserted sustaining effect remains source-attributed; creatures are the antecedent of they.

56.189.8: Both witnesses retain humans as subject, properly, through this, their own level and aspect of Torah. Do not conflate this with the preceding animals remaining at their level. Independent review: Sit renders יושבים without deciding legal details of dwelling; the humans, not the animals of the prior sentence, occupy this level.

56.189.9: Preserve both quotations, Do not, the maternal Torah/Binah link, and chapter-only references Proverbs1 and2, without adding verse numbers. Correction to the initial apparatus: only the pointed field gives אִם as if; the unpointed אם is not pointed and admits mother/if wordplay. The selected If follows supplied אִם, not proof of an authorially prior reading. Simchas Torah names the celebration; its explanatory English gloss in the secondary is not a source bracket. selected.translationSourceEnglish: (56.) See this — I found in the handwriting of Rabbainu o.b.m. himself, regarding the Torah "And he built him a house" (Likutay Moharan, Torah 266): Know — when the world blemishes the mitzvah of Sukkah, when they do not fulfill it as is proper, they cause death or illness to the animals and other living creatures — everything according to the blemish. For this is the difference between human beings and other living creatures: the bounty of human beings is drawn from the place of [the Sefirah of] Binah, as our Sages of blessed memory said [Brachos 10]: that He made breasts for her in the place of Binah — which is not the case with other living creatures, whose bounty is drawn from the place of the private parts. And the aspect of Sukkah is the aspect of mother (Binah) who covers (d'mesakekhah) her children, and we draw from her — and through this mitzvah we are distinguished from the bounty of other living creatures. And when one blemishes the mitzvah of Sukkah, one then descends through this from the level of humans, and there is no bounty for them from the place of Binah, and they descend to the levels of other living creatures. And the other living creatures are displaced from their bounty, since the humans take their bounty — and then the living creatures die or fall ill — everything according to how much bounty was taken from them, whether much or little. And this is [Genesis 33:17]: "And for his cattle he built booths (sukkos)" — that is, for Sukkos is life and sustenance for the living creatures, that they remain on their level as mentioned above. And when humans sit in the Sukkos properly, through this they are on their level, and in the aspect of Torah. For the Torah is the aspect of [Proverbs 1:8]: "Do not forsake the Torah of your mother (imekha)," [Proverbs 2:3]: "If you call to Binah." Because of this, adjacent to Sukkos we celebrate Simchat Torah [the rejoicing with the Torah]. And this [is the acronym]: vayaakov nasa Sukkosah vaYiven — the initial letters: Sivan — for in Sivan the Torah was given, and we are on the level of the Torah through the mitzvah of Sukkah as mentioned above.

retained_baseline.he: (נו) ראה זה מצאתי מכתב יד רבנו זכרונו לברכה בעצמו מענין התורה ויבן לו בית בסימן רס"ו דע כשהעולם פוגמין במצות סכה כשאין מקימין אותה כראוי גורמין מיתה או חולאת לבהמות ולשאר בעלי חיים הכל לפי הפגם. כי זה ההפרש שבין בני האדם ובין בעלי חיים כי שפעם של בני אדם יונקים ממקום בינה, כמאמר חכמינו זכרונם לברכה (ברכות י): שעשה לה דדים במקום בינה, מה שאין כן בעלי חיים, ששפעם יונקים ממקום הערוה. ובחינת סכה היא בחינת אמא בינה דמסככא על בנהא ואנו יונקים ממנה, ובזאת המצוה אנו מבדלים משפע של בעלי חיים. וכשפוגמין במצות סכה אזי יורדין על ידי זה ממדרגת בני אדם, ואין להם שפע ממקום בינה, ויורדין למדרגות שאר בעלי חיים. ונדחין שאר בעלי חיים מהשפע שלהם, כיון שבני אדם לוקחין השפע שלהם, ואזי הבעלי החיים מתים או נופלים בחלאים הכל לפי לקיחת השפע שלהם אם רב אם מעט, וזהו (בראשית ל"ג) ולמקנהו עשה סכת. הינו כי סכות הוא חיים וקיום לבעלי חיים שישארו על מדרגתם כנ"ל. וכשבני אדם יושבים בסכות כראוי, על ידי זה הם במדרגתן, ובבחינת תורה. כי התורה היא בחינת (משלי א): "אל תטש תורת אמך", "אם לבינה תקרא". (שם ב) בשביל זה סמוך לסכות אנו עושים שמחת תורה. וזה סוון ראשי תבות ו'יעקב נ'סע ס'כותה ו'יבן כי בסיון נתנה תורה ואנו במדרגת התורה על ידי מצות סכה כנזכר לעיל:
retained_baseline.en:
Sichos HaShayachim l'Sipuray Ma'asiyos
  General articles 60–73  |  Section sub-numbers 1–14 60.
    (Section sub-number 1)
  
  
    (1.) The story of the Burgher he told after someone had told him beforehand about writing with golden letters — and this was after Purim 5569 [1809]. Before Purim he told the story of the Wise Man and the Simple Man. 61.
    (Section sub-number 2)
  
  
    (2.) On the night after the Sabbath of the Torah portion Noach, in the year 5570 [1809]: after he had said on the Sabbath night the Torah that begins [Likutay Moharan, vol. 2, Torah 67]: "And this is the aspect of a eulogy for the passing of the tzaddik" — and on the night after the Sabbath we entered to him as was our custom, and he motioned with his hand that we should leave from him, and we immediately left from him. And it was a wonder to us, for it was our constant custom to speak with him a great deal on the night after the Sabbath, and we had a bit of sorrow from this, and we entered the house of the local rav. After some hours he sent his servant, who called us to come in to him, and I and my colleague Rabbi Naftoli entered to him. And he commanded us to tell him news — as was his constant custom, that he always asked specifically to be told news — and Rabbi Naftoli told him what he had heard then about the war of France, which was happening at that time. And then in that conversation we were marveling and astonished at the great rise of one who had arisen so suddenly, for he had at first been a simple slave and became emperor. And we spoke with him then about this. He answered and said: Who knows what soul he has — for it is possible that [the soul] was exchanged, for so it is that sometimes in the Heichalay HaTemuroas [the "Heavenly Chambers of Exchange"] souls are exchanged etc. And afterwards he began to tell that there had already been such an incident — that once a queen gave birth, and at that same time etc. — and he told the entire story of the prince who was exchanged. After he told the story of the king's son and the maidservant's son, I had an argument with my colleague Rabbi Naftoli regarding what is written there — that when he went to the fair, he took everything he had and left it at the inn.

(שָׁם ב) בִּשְׁבִיל זֶה סָמוּךְ לְסֻכּוֹת אָנוּ עוֹשִׂים שִׂמְחַת תּוֹרָה. וְזֶה סִוָון רָאשֵׁי־תֵבוֹת וְ'יַעֲקֹב נָ'סַע סֻ'כּוֹתָה וַ'יִּבֶן כִּי בְּסִיוָן נִתְּנָה תּוֹרָה וְאָנוּ בְּמַדְרֵגַת הַתּוֹרָה עַל־יְדֵי מִצְוַת סֻכָּה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל:

selected.he: (נז) דע שעל ידי מצוות סכה כראוי מתר לו לעסק בבנין ואינו מזיק לו לממונו כי אמרו רבותינו זכרונם לברכה (יבמות צ"ג): העוסק בבנין מתמסכן. וטעם הדבר כי מה ענין העניות להבונה, אך טעם הדבר כי מי שבונה בנין צריך לבנות בחכמה, כמו שכתוב (משלי כ"ד): "בחכמה יבנה בית" ובודאי הבונה בחכמה לא יתמסכן ואדרבא יתעשר ויתקים בו בחכמה יבנה בית וכו' ובדעת חדרים ימלאו. אבל מי שבונה בלא חכמה מענישין אותו בעניות, ועל ידי זה יתבזה חכמתו בבחינת (קהלת ט): "חכמת המסכן בזויה", מדה כנגד מדה. ועל ידי מצוות סכה הוא במדרגת תורה כנ"ל והתורה היא מקור כל החכמות בשביל זה מתר לו לבנות, כי בודאי יש לו חכמה, וסימן לדבר ויעקב נסע סכתה ויבן על ידי מצוות סכה התר לו לבנות לב ראשי תבות ל'ו ב'ית. לב זו התורה בית מבראשית, למד מלעיני כל ישראל, הינו כלל התורה וכו':

selected.en: (57) Know that through the commandments of sukkah, properly [fulfilled], it is permitted for him to engage in building, and it does not harm his money; for our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Yevamot 93): One who engages in building becomes impoverished. And the reason for the matter—for what connection does poverty have with the builder? But the reason for the matter is that one who builds a building needs to build with wisdom, as it is written (Proverbs 24): ‘With wisdom a house shall be built.’ And certainly one who builds with wisdom will not become impoverished; on the contrary, he will become wealthy, and it will be fulfilled in him: ‘With wisdom a house shall be built,’ etc., ‘and with knowledge the chambers shall be filled.’ But one who builds without wisdom—they punish him with poverty, and through this his wisdom will be despised, in the aspect of (Ecclesiastes 9): ‘The wisdom of the poor man is despised,’ measure for measure. And through the commandments of sukkah he is at the level of Torah, as mentioned above, and the Torah is the source of all wisdoms. For this reason it is permitted for him to build, for certainly he has wisdom. And a sign for the matter: ‘And Jacob journeyed to Sukkos and built’—through the commandments of sukkah he was permitted to build. Lev (heart) is the initial letters of ל'ו ב'ית, lo bayis (‘for himself a house’). Lev is the Torah: bet from ‘Bereshis’ (‘In the beginning’), lamed from ‘le-einei kol Yisrael’ (‘before the eyes of all Israel’), that is, the entirety of the Torah, etc.:

selected.translationSourceEnglish: (57.) Know — through the mitzvah of Sukkah as is proper, it is permitted for him to engage in construction and it does not harm his money, for our Rabbis of blessed memory said [Yevamos 63]: "One who engages in building becomes impoverished." And the rationale of the matter: what does poverty have to do with building? But the rationale of the matter is: one who builds a structure needs to build with wisdom, as it is written [Proverbs 24:3]: "With wisdom a house is built" — and certainly one who builds with wisdom will not become impoverished, and on the contrary, will become wealthy, and the verse [ibid.] will be fulfilled in him: "With wisdom a house is built ... and with knowledge the chambers are filled." But one who builds without wisdom is punished with poverty, and through this his wisdom is despised, in the aspect of [Ecclesiastes 9:16]: "the wisdom of the poor man is despised" — measure for measure. And through the mitzvah of Sukkah he is on the level of Torah as mentioned above, and the Torah is the source of all wisdoms — therefore it is permitted for him to build, for certainly he has wisdom. And the sign of the matter: "And Jacob traveled to Sukkos and built" — the initial letters of lo vaYiven ["lev" = heart] — heart [is] Torah. The letter lamed [comes] from "before the eyes of all Israel" [the end of the Torah]; the mem from "in the beginning" [the beginning of the Torah] — that is, the entirety of the Torah etc.

retained_baseline.en:
And one of us thought he left it there because of what he owed at the inn, while the other said no — he simply left it there. And we made a wager on this and went and asked his holy mouth. And he was then occupied with his service [of G-d] and was walking back and forth in his house as his holy custom, and he answered us according to the words of the second one — that he left it simply, not on account of a debt. Afterwards there was with him one distinguished man of our men, and Rabbainu o.b.m. spoke with him and told him that in these stories, when a single word is changed from how he himself said it, a great deal is lacking from the story. And he told him: Consider these two who made the wager about the aforementioned matter — it seems at first glance that this is a small thing, and there is not so much to be particular about whether it is as this one says or as that one says. And in truth a great deal depends on this, and there is great particularity and precision in it. And from this you can understand somewhat how far — how far — these stories reach, for his thoughts were extremely deep. Fortunate is he who merits to attain something of them according to his level. 62.

selected.en: A story of one man among the men of the Baal Shem Tov, of blessed memory, who was ill and had become very weak, and sent a certain man to the Baal Shem Tov, of blessed memory, to ask the Baal Shem Tov, of blessed memory, to travel to him. That is, that the Baal Shem Tov, of blessed memory, should travel to the sick man. And so it was. And the aforementioned man, the messenger, came to the Baal Shem Tov, of blessed memory, and told him all the aforementioned: that this man is ill, and that he had asked him to travel to him; and the Baal Shem Tov, of blessed memory, traveled to him.

retained_baseline.en: He answered and said to the cantor: Are you not the baal tefillah through whom everything is drawn (that is, all the Divine bounties) — so why do you not have a garment (called a kaftan)? And in the meanwhile he began to tell it in these words: There was already such a case — that there was a baal tefillah — and he told the entire story. And at the beginning of his telling we did not know that he was telling a story from his stories, but rather we thought he was telling a story that had simply occurred. Only afterwards, when he entered into the words, we understood the awesome nature of what he was telling — that it is an awesome story from his stories, which are stories of primordial years.

displaced_english.text: He answered and said to the cantor: Are you not the baal tefillah through whom everything is drawn (that is, all the Divine bounties) — so why do you not have a garment (called a kaftan)? And in the meanwhile he began to tell it in these words: There was already such a case — that there was a baal tefillah — and he told the entire story. And at the beginning of his telling we did not know that he was telling a story from his stories, but rather we thought he was telling a story that had simply occurred. Only afterwards, when he entered into the words, we understood the awesome nature of what he was telling — that it is an awesome story from his stories, which are stories of primordial years.

selected.he: בדרך שאל האיש השליח להבעל שם טוב זכרונו לברכה, איך ששמעתי מכם שכשאדם עושה תשובה שלמה בודאי לא ימות קדם זמנו. וזה האיש החולה כמדמה שעשה תשובה שלמה באמת והוא איש כשר באמת, ועדין לא בא בימים כל כך, ומפני מה לא יתרפא מחליו. השיב הבעל שם טוב זכרונו לברכה להשליח אמת כך אמרתי ובודאי כן הוא וזה האיש החולה הנ"ל גם כן עשה תשובה שלמה באמת על כל חטאיו. וזה שלא נתרפא עדין הוא מחמת שלא התודה חטאיו לפני צדיק אמתי וזה שאני נוסע אליו בכדי שיתודה, ובאם שיתודה לפני תכף יתרפא, ובאם שלא ירצה להתודות לפני תכף יכבד עליו חליו ויתחיל לצעק אוי ואבוי על כל איבריו וידיו ורגליו וימות.

selected.en: On the way, the man, the messenger, asked the Baal Shem Tov, of blessed memory: How [is this]? I heard from you that when a person performs complete repentance, certainly he will not die before his time. And this sick man, it seems, has performed complete repentance in truth, and he is an upright man in truth, and he is not yet so advanced in years; why does he not recover from his illness? The Baal Shem Tov, of blessed memory, answered the messenger: True, thus I said, and certainly it is so; and this aforementioned sick man has also performed complete repentance in truth for all his sins. And his not yet having recovered is because he has not confessed his sins before a true tzaddik; and this is why I am traveling to him, so that he may confess. And if he confesses before me, he will recover immediately; and if he does not wish to confess before me, immediately his illness will grow heavier upon him, and he will begin to cry ‘Woe and alas’ over all his limbs and his hands and his feet, and he will die.

selected.translationSourceEnglish: On the road, the messenger asked the Baal Shem Tov o.b.m.: I heard from you that when a person does complete repentance, certainly he will not die before his time. And this sick man — it seems that he has done complete repentance in truth, and he is a truly upright man, and he has not yet reached old age — so why does he not recover from his illness? The Baal Shem Tov o.b.m. answered the messenger: True — that is what I said, and certainly it is so, and this sick man mentioned above has also truly done complete repentance on all his sins. And the reason he has not yet recovered is because he has not confessed his sins before a true tzaddik — and this is why I am traveling to him, so that he should confess, and if he confesses before me, he will immediately recover. And if he does not wish to confess before me, immediately his illness will become heavier upon him, and he will begin to cry out "Woe and alas" over all his limbs and hands and feet, and he will die.

selected.en: For in truth, in the upper worlds—that is, in the court above—there is no sin or transgression upon him at all, because he has performed complete repentance for all the sins, as one must do. And after his passing, the kelippot (husks) and the external forces will have no hold on him, for he has already rectified all that he blemished. And if he confesses before me, then he will recover immediately; and if he does not confess, then the external forces still have power to take vengeance upon him in this world, in all his body and his limbs, until he dies.

selected.he: וכן הוה שבא אליו הבעל שם טוב זכרונו לברכה ואמר להחולה בזה הלשון אמר מה שאתה יודע, והקדוש ברוך הוא יודע ואני יודע גם כן, הינו שיתודה לפניו כל החטאים. ואמר לו כך שלשה פעמים ולא רצה לומר. ותכף התחיל לצעק אוי ואבוי על גדל כאב כל איבריו וצעק בתמרורים בפרוטרוט על כאב כל איבר ואיבר מאיבריו, כי התחילו להשבר שקורין ברעכין כל עצמותיו של כל איבר ואיבר, וצעק כך מתוך חליו איזה זמן עד שמת כמו שאמר הבעל שם טוב זכרונו לברכה.

selected.en: And so it was: the Baal Shem Tov, of blessed memory, came to him and said to the sick man in these words: ‘Say what you know, and the Holy One, blessed be He, knows, and I too know’—that is, that he should confess before him all the sins. And he said this to him three times, and [the sick man] did not wish to say [it]. And immediately he began to cry ‘Woe and alas’ over the great pain of all his limbs, and cried bitterly, in detail, over the pain of each and every one of his limbs, for all his bones of each and every limb began to break, which they call brekhin; and he cried thus in the midst of his illness for some time until he died, as the Baal Shem Tov, of blessed memory, had said.

retained_baseline.he: וכן הוה שבא אליו הבעל שם טוב זכרונו לברכה ואמר להחולה בזה הלשון אמר מה שאתה יודע, והקדוש ברוך הוא יודע ואני יודע גם כן, הינו שיתודה לפניו כל החטאים. ואמר לו כך שלשה פעמים ולא רצה לומר. ותכף התחיל לצעק אוי ואבוי על גדל כאב כל איבריו וצעק בתמרורים בפרוטרוט על כאב כל איבר ואיבר מאיבריו, כי התחילו להשבר שקורין ברעכין כל עצמותיו של כל איבר ואיבר, וצעק כך מתוך חליו איזה זמן עד שמת כמו שאמר הבעל שם טוב זכרונו לברכה.
retained_baseline.en: Afterwards, when they were about to sacrifice [me], I changed my mind and I wanted to hide — but I saw that the entire multitude was surrounding me and it was impossible to hide. And I wanted to go out of the city, and I was going out and leaving the city — but in the midst of going out I turned back and came into the city again. And I looked and saw that I had turned back and come into the city. And I wanted to hide among the Moscow people [Palk Maskviter — Muscovites], but I thought to myself: if the whole world were to come and demand from them that they hand me over, they would certainly hand me over to them.

required_qualification_occurrences.text: 51.177.10: One learned from another, the growing breach and our many sins remain. As though permitted translates the comparative כ in כהתר and the affected them; it is not a legal permission. The entire clause is absent from the secondary witness.

required_qualification_occurrences.text: 51.177.11: Even now, truly upright, do not shave their beards, and even in Ashkenaz preserve both emphases and negation. required_qualification_occurrences.text: 51.178.1: Even, adjoining countries, not yet and as in Ashkenaz are preserved: this negates equivalent spread, not all nearby occurrence. The entire opening is absent from secondary. Both Hebrew witnesses, including their agreement forms, remain exact.

required_qualification_occurrences.text: 51.178.2: Somewhat upright takes קצת with הכשרים, contextually contrasting the truly upright of177.11. required_qualification_occurrences.text: 51.178.5: The One who examines hearts, most rather than all, deliberately, defiantly and with a razor remain the source's accusation. required_qualification_occurrences.text: 52.179.1: Both Hebrew fields name Likutay Tinyana and section ל"ב; tzaddikim means righteous persons. required_qualification_occurrences.text: 52.179.2: תקס"ט לפ"ק [לפרט קטן] is preserved as the Hebrew-year designation with its explicit abbreviation/gloss; the conventional millennium is supplied in 5569. required_qualification_occurrences.text: 52.179.3: Independent review supersedes the initial preference for first/beforehand. וספר מעשה מקדם / וְסִפֵּר מַעֲשֶׂה מִקֹּדֶם is selected as he related a story from earlier times; alternatively, he related the story beforehand, before the Torah. required_qualification_occurrences.text: 52.179.4: בעל דרשיר / בַּעַל דַּרְשֶׁיר is retained as baal darshir with the source’s own הינו דרשן gloss; למטה means lower down, without asserting a precise seating plan.

required_qualification_occurrences.text: 52.180.1: התחילו is restored as began; להפציר marks urging, not a neutral invitation. Before them retains the audience.

required_qualification_occurrences.text: 52.180.2: גם כן repeats the guests’ purpose of mockery; the Baal Shem Tov’s place at the head is explicit, but no prohibition on speaking Torah is supplied.

required_qualification_occurrences.text: 52.180.3: בתמימותו is simplicity/wholeheartedness. The secondary addition as was befitting him has no explicit counterpart and is removed; the preacher’s agency and beginning to speak remain.
required_qualification_occurrences.placement: inside complete translationProvenance directly after selected English

required_qualification_occurrences.text: 52.180.4: בתוך פסת ידיהם / בְּתוֹךְ פִּסַּת יְדֵיהֶם is retained as into the palms of their hands; it plausibly conveys concealed or stifled laughter, but no closed fists or precise gesture is asserted. לאחוכא ואטלולא / לְאִחוּכָא וְאִטְלוּלָא and the source’s bracketed [לשחוק וליצנות] / [לְשְׂחוֹק וְלֵיצָנוּת] are both translated. Independent review corrects the initial note’s nonexistent quoted הוא: the actual wording is והיה / וְהָיָה, whose unexpressed subject is read contextually as the preacher; his discourse or the situation is grammatically possible. Pointing does not settle this agency.
required_qualification_occurrences.placement: inside complete translationProvenance directly after selected English

required_qualification_occurrences.text: 52.180.5: The narrator reports the preacher’s understanding of their motive. This preserves the food-related reason rather than substituting presumed inadequacy of his teaching.

required_qualification_occurrences.text: 52.180.6: אין יכולים is impersonal plural, rendered one cannot, not a personal confession of inability. The rhetorical question preserves the negation, prohibition and piece of fish; its recurrence in unit 181 is retained.

required_qualification_occurrences.text: 52.180.7: הקפיד וכעס comprises two reactions, retained as took exception and became angry. עליהם refers contextually to the mocking guests, not the preacher; this is a contextual identification, not established by pointing alone.

required_qualification_occurrences.text: 52.180.8: והוטב בעיניו מאד is favorable reception with מאד retained; the contextual subject remains the Baal Shem Tov. No independent claim about the quality of the discourse is substituted for his judgment.

required_qualification_occurrences.text: 52.180.9: אומר is present says; מפי אליהו is retained literally from the mouth of Elijah as the Baal Shem Tov’s attributed claim, not independently authenticated revelation.
required_qualification_occurrences.placement: inside complete translationProvenance directly after selected English

required_qualification_occurrences.text: 52.180.10: The closing all this explicitly attributes the entire foregoing account to Rabbainu, not only the remark about Elijah; the attribution is not omitted.
required_qualification_occurrences.placement: inside complete translationProvenance directly after selected English

required_qualification_occurrences.text: 52.181.1: The repeated rhetorical quotation is retained in full. אינם here differs from אין in unit 180; both express impersonal inability, not a newly assigned speaker. This favorable judgment is Rabbainu’s, distinct from the Baal Shem Tov’s earlier judgment.
required_qualification_occurrences.placement: inside complete translationProvenance directly after selected English

required_qualification_occurrences.text: 52.181.2: The subsequent delivery of the aforementioned Torah follows the repeated quotation. שיודעים is present know; והם is and they, not an unmarked adversative but. Hidden is repeated as in both Hebrew fields.
required_qualification_occurrences.placement: inside complete translationProvenance directly after selected English

required_qualification_occurrences.text: 52.181.3: Independent review corrects the initial apparatus citation ידע: the supplied text actually reads שהיה יודע / שֶׁהָיָה יוֹדֵעַ, a past state (who knew), contrasting with the general present שיודעים / שֶׁיּוֹדְעִים in the preceding group. אך / אַךְ remains but; wondrous Torah, hidden tzaddik and the world’s mockery are repeated in full. העולם / הָעוֹלָם is collective with התלוצצו / הִתְלוֹצְצוּ plural; no Hebrew grammar is silently normalized.
required_qualification_occurrences.placement: inside complete translationProvenance directly after selected English

required_qualification_occurrences.text: 53.182.1: תקס"ח is the supplied year designation (568 with the conventional millennium understood in 5568); the secondary Gregorian [1807] is removed because neither Hebrew field supplies it. Close to Rosh Hashana is retained without deciding which side of the festival. אני is the narrator and וחברי is my companion, not an unnamed collective.
required_qualification_occurrences.placement: inside complete translationProvenance directly after selected English

required_qualification_occurrences.text: 53.182.2: שחלם לו frames the ensuing conversation as the content of his dream, not a second witnessed waking conversation. The text leaves the conversing group implicit. כי is retained as for. The secondary [Exodus 15:26] is editorial identification only, not printed in either Hebrew witness; it is kept here as an editorial reference rather than in the translated main text.
required_qualification_occurrences.placement: inside complete translationProvenance directly after selected English

required_qualification_occurrences.text: 53.182.2.IR: באשר שהיו משיחים / בַּאֲשֶׁר שֶׁהָיוּ מְשִׂיחִים is read as the circumstance/content of the dream (that they were conversing), not a new waking event or an additional unexpressed cause. The sin in מְשִׂיחִים supports conversing. The dream-teller is contextually Rabbainu; neither the singular verbs nor supplied vowels name him.
required_qualification_occurrences.placement: inside complete translationProvenance directly after selected English

required_qualification_occurrences.text: 53.182.3: ורק repeats the preceding לבד and is retained as and only, with present ability יכול. This is the assertion reported in the dream, not an independent medical assertion by the editor.
required_qualification_occurrences.placement: inside complete translationProvenance directly after selected English

required_qualification_occurrences.text: 53.182.4: רוצה is wishes/wants, with no expressed infinitival object. [To heal] is the minimal contextual supply and is visibly bracketed; the question does not negate divine ability or assert unwillingness.
required_qualification_occurrences.placement: inside complete translationProvenance directly after selected English

required_qualification_occurrences.text: 53.182.5: אחד משנינו / אֶחָד מִשְּׁנֵינוּ means one of us two, the narrator and Rabbi Naftoli, without identifying the respondent. ולא רצה להגיד מי האחד / וְלֹא רָצָה לְהַגִּיד מִי הָאֶחָד is selected as the dream-teller’s refusal to disclose who answered. [Rabbainu] is an editorial contextual identification, not a source name here; the nearer respondent is also a grammatically possible subject. The pointed masculine singular does not resolve that choice. English dashes make a narrative aside but are editorial punctuation, not parentheses present in the Hebrew.
required_qualification_occurrences.placement: inside complete translationProvenance directly after selected English

required_qualification_occurrences.text: 53.182.6: Exact letter-marked witnesses: כ'י א'ני ה' ר'ופאך / כִּ'י אֲ'נִי ה' ר'וֹפְאֶךָ and א'מן כ'ן י'הי ר'צון / אָ'מֵן כֵּ'ן יְ'הִי רָ'צוֹן. In displayed order their Hebrew consonantal initials are כ–א–ה–ר versus א–כ–י–ר. Reversing the first two and invoking a yod-initial divine name in place of the displayed ה' would explain a correspondence, but neither operation is silently performed, and this is not authentication of the intended mechanism. The source’s ראשי תבות / רָאשֵׁי־תֵבוֹת assertion remains an attributed, qualified claim, not a verified ordered acrostic. מורה על זה כי הוא / מוֹרֶה עַל־זֶה כִּי הוּא is represented explicitly. Independent review renders רצון / רָצוֹן as the noun will: Amen, so may it be [His] will; [His] is an editorial contextual supply. The transliterations and parenthesized English glosses are editorial aids, not source parentheses. Supplied vowels and apostrophe positions are preserved, not asserted authorial.
required_qualification_occurrences.placement: inside complete translationProvenance directly after selected English

required_qualification_occurrences.text: 53.182.7: The exact closing reference כנדפס בלקוטי תנינא סימן מ"ב / כַּנִּדְפַּס בְּלִקּוּטֵי תִּנְיָנָא סִימָן מ"ב is retained as as printed in Likutay Tinyana, section 42. source.text: a story is recounted of Rabbi Nachman, on the day before the last Rosh Hashana of his life, someone asked him for advice how to merit to diligence in Torah study. Rabbi Nachman told him that he should not speak (bad) of any Jew (see the explanation there, and Sichos Huran 91). The person asked Rabbainu, what if he sees that he is a completely wicked person? Rabbainu strongly admonished him, how he could suggest that one from (the nation of) Israel is completely wicked, for certainly there is still found in him a bit of good or some good point where he is not wicked, and he recalled the matter of, "a bit more and there is no wicked" which is explained in the Torah-lesson of Azamru, see there. Based on this, Saba wrote in Blossoms of the Spring (volume 3, letter 268. In the early printings see volume 2, letter 119), "Also he should be careful not to speak (bad) of any one of (the nation of) Israel, just on the contrary, he should strive with all this strength to find merit and good in each one of Israel; and even if he seems Heaven forbid, to be completely wicked, he should strive to find in him good points where he is not wicked, until every one of Israel is beautiful and pleasant in his eyes."

Also see The Life of Our Leader Rabbi Nachman 48, about when a very famous rabbi visited Rabbainu a year before his passing, Rabbanu didn't want to deliver Torah, see there.

source.text:
Sichos HaShayachim l'Sipuray Ma'asiyos
  General articles 60–73  |  Section sub-numbers 1–14 60.
    (Section sub-number 1)
  
  
    (1.) The story of the Burgher he told after someone had told him beforehand about writing with golden letters — and this was after Purim 5569 [1809]. Before Purim he told the story of the Wise Man and the Simple Man. 61.
    (Section sub-number 2)
  
  
    (2.) On the night after the Sabbath of the Torah portion Noach, in the year 5570 [1809]: after he had said on the Sabbath night the Torah that begins [Likutay Moharan, vol. 2, Torah 67]: "And this is the aspect of a eulogy for the passing of the tzaddik" — and on the night after the Sabbath we entered to him as was our custom, and he motioned with his hand that we should leave from him, and we immediately left from him. And it was a wonder to us, for it was our constant custom to speak with him a great deal on the night after the Sabbath, and we had a bit of sorrow from this, and we entered the house of the local rav. After some hours he sent his servant, who called us to come in to him, and I and my colleague Rabbi Naftoli entered to him. And he commanded us to tell him news — as was his constant custom, that he always asked specifically to be told news — and Rabbi Naftoli told him what he had heard then about the war of France, which was happening at that time. And then in that conversation we were marveling and astonished at the great rise of one who had arisen so suddenly, for he had at first been a simple slave and became emperor. And we spoke with him then about this. He answered and said: Who knows what soul he has — for it is possible that [the soul] was exchanged, for so it is that sometimes in the Heichalay HaTemuroas [the "Heavenly Chambers of Exchange"] souls are exchanged etc. And afterwards he began to tell that there had already been such an incident — that once a queen gave birth, and at that same time etc. — and he told the entire story of the prince who was exchanged. After he told the story of the king's son and the maidservant's son, I had an argument with my colleague Rabbi Naftoli regarding what is written there — that when he went to the fair, he took everything he had and left it at the inn.

source.text:
And one of us thought he left it there because of what he owed at the inn, while the other said no — he simply left it there. And we made a wager on this and went and asked his holy mouth. And he was then occupied with his service [of G-d] and was walking back and forth in his house as his holy custom, and he answered us according to the words of the second one — that he left it simply, not on account of a debt. Afterwards there was with him one distinguished man of our men, and Rabbainu o.b.m. spoke with him and told him that in these stories, when a single word is changed from how he himself said it, a great deal is lacking from the story. And he told him: Consider these two who made the wager about the aforementioned matter — it seems at first glance that this is a small thing, and there is not so much to be particular about whether it is as this one says or as that one says. And in truth a great deal depends on this, and there is great particularity and precision in it. And from this you can understand somewhat how far — how far — these stories reach, for his thoughts were extremely deep. Fortunate is he who merits to attain something of them according to his level. 62.
    (Section sub-number 3)
  
  
    (3.) The story of the Baal Tefillah (Master of Prayer) began after he had a conversation with the cantor Rabbi Yosef of this [town], and we were standing before him, and the aforementioned cantor's garment was torn.

source.text: He answered and said to the cantor: Are you not the baal tefillah through whom everything is drawn (that is, all the Divine bounties) — so why do you not have a garment (called a kaftan)? And in the meanwhile he began to tell it in these words: There was already such a case — that there was a baal tefillah — and he told the entire story. And at the beginning of his telling we did not know that he was telling a story from his stories, but rather we thought he was telling a story that had simply occurred. Only afterwards, when he entered into the words, we understood the awesome nature of what he was telling — that it is an awesome story from his stories, which are stories of primordial years.
